long_biography.plain_text:
Jet Aviation grew from a Basel aircraft-maintenance operation founded by Carl W. Hirschmann into a global business-aviation group, adding charter, aircraft management, cabin completions and ground handling. After his death, ownership remained with his widow Rita and their descendants, while governance was complicated by years of family and foundation disputes.

In 2003, Rita Hirschmann took the chair of Hirschmann Industrial Holding, Jet Aviation’s parent, after Moritz Suter’s brief tenure. Contemporary reporting described her as the family’s forceful figure at 77, though her chairmanship was short. The family ultimately agreed to sell Jet Aviation to Permira in 2005, closing the Hirschmann era at a company that then employed about 3,500 people worldwide.
